source.title: The Linear Geometry of Interpretable Tokens: Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses for Unlearned Diffusion Models
source.authors: Siyi Chen; Yimeng Zhang; Sijia Liu; Qing Qu

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether diffusion unlearning leaves target concepts recoverable through attacks, and reports a projection-based defense that reduces—but does not eliminate—attack success. Its results refine and challenge the idea that unlearning reliably removes the concept.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own attack success rates (ASR) for unlearned diffusion models and for models after its projection-based defense. The NoAttack values are the reported baseline for the attack comparisons. It does not test fine-tuning the unlearned model on a small relearning set, low-bit quantization, or recovery by rephrasing prompts, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information. SubAttack learns attack-token embeddings using target-concept images; it is not a test of fine-tuning the model on unrelated or loosely related examples. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. Duplicate or overlapping attack tables and auxiliary results are not included.
record.test_reason: New setting: concept-erasure unlearning in Stable Diffusion v1.4 (ESD, FMN, UCE, SPM, MACE, SA, AC, SalUn and EraseDiff, plus RECE). The study runs its own attacks and reports attack success rates (ASR) for regenerating the erased concept, with NoAttack baselines. The SubAttack rows bear on whether unlearning resists attack (A). SubAttack on RECE, and the authors' own SubDefense under re-optimized attacks, bear on robust counter-methods (F). Two further results appear only in the text. Its reruns of UnlearnDiff, a discrete adversarial-prompt jailbreak, bear on E. Its analysis of what the attack tokens encode bears on C's 'blocks access rather than deleting'. SubAttack is a white-box token embedding learned from target-concept images. It is not weight fine-tuning, quantization or a typed prompt, so B and D are untested and the SubAttack rows are not linked to E.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Unlearned diffusion models retain a coherent, interpretable, attack-accessible linear residual of the erased concept in token-embedding space. SubAttack reads it out, with higher ASR and transferability than UnlearnDiff and CCE. SubDefense projects it out, lowering ASR while preserving utility better than RECE. The authors stress that this is not complete erasure: residual attack success and a rank-utility trade-off remain.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Stable Diffusion v1.4 unlearning methods and develops SubAttack by learning token embeddings from target-concept images; it is not an LLM unlearning or fine-tuning recovery test. SubDefense projects directions from the CLIP token-embedding vocabulary.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack recovery varies by model and target concept. SubDefense outcomes depend on the chosen projection rank; the paper reports that increasing rank reduces ASR while harming generation utility.
record.problems: Evaluation primarily uses Stable Diffusion v1.4 with a CLIP text encoder and assumes white-box access plus target-concept images. ASR depends on imperfect concept classifiers. Base unlearning does not bring all model-concept settings close to chance. SubDefense leaves residual attack success in many settings and trades robustness against generation utility.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted separate UnlearnDiff and CCE comparison values from Tables 3, 4, 5, 14, and 15; detailed I2P, transfer, reproducibility, and exploratory black-box attack results in Tables 2, 12-20, and 22-23; attack and defense ablations in Tables 25-28; and qualitative figures. These are overlapping attack comparisons, defense settings, or auxiliary analyses beyond the selected SubAttack and SubDefense rows.

untested.parts: LLM targeted-knowledge accuracy and preservation of general ability. The study measures image-concept ASR in diffusion models. COCO FID/CLIP utility is reported only for ESD and UCE, and only in the defense experiments.
All: no relearning by fine-tuning model weights.
Ablation of an internal activation direction. The analysis concerns input-side token-embedding associations, not UNet or text-encoder activations.

Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information. Only optimized discrete adversarial prompts (UnlearnDiff) are run against NoAttack baselines. Ring-A-Bell, a black-box prompt attack, appears only in the defense table, with no unattacked baseline.
Resistance of SubDefense or RECE to fine-tuning, quantization or activation-ablation attacks. Only SubAttack, UnlearnDiff, CCE and Ring-A-Bell are tested.

missing.what: SubAttack on the adversarially fine-tuned unlearner STEREO, a robust counter-method: nudity ASR 21.67%, falling to 6.67% with SubDefense at 20 directions. No unattacked STEREO baseline is given.

Interpretability analysis of what remains after unlearning. Strongly unlearned models mute explicit keywords such as 'nude', but SubAttack embeddings built from implicit tokens still regenerate the concept. Those embeddings transfer back to the original SD at 84-98% ASR, which the authors read as residual associations inherited from SD.

UnlearnDiff (discrete adversarial-prompt jailbreak) ASR on unlearned models vs NoAttack. Examples: UCE nudity 23 to 78.22%, UCE church 6.55 to 61.67%, ESD Van Gogh 5.78 to 40.94%, FMN church 51.56 to 35.33%; on I2P nudity, ESD 20.56 to 74.47%. rows_left_out declares these as comparison values, but they are the study's only evidence on E.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) The refused range item is expanded into one row_fixes item per row, R01-R53. Every row carried undeclared V1/V3/V6 and is relinked by what it measures.
(2) Row states are now read against each version's own effect, as the rules' state table requires and sibling verdicts in this run do. For A, an attack that restores the concept means A's effect is absent. The earlier verdict used 'observed' for recovery, which clashed with its 'challenges' label. Cutoffs: from a low baseline, SubAttack ASR above 50% is absent and 11-50% is partial. Rows with NoAttack at 40-90% are absent but grouped under a limits_scope label, because A's near-chance premise fails before any attack (R07, R14 and R29 were cannot_determine).
(3) Two rows join the A challenges group, for consistency with R13, R31 and R39: R19 (SPM nudity, NoAttack 22.56%) leaves the high-baseline group, and R30 (AC Van Gogh, 61.67%) leaves the modest-recovery group.
(4) R39-R41 (RECE, a robustness refinement of UCE) are also linked to F, with a new F challenges label.
(5) R50 (UCE church, 3.22% after SubDefense) is set to observed, with a new narrow F supports label.
(6) C: the earlier verdict listed a C missing item but gave no C verdict and called C untested. A text-based C supports label is added for the 'blocks access rather than deleting' clause.
(7) E: the earlier verdict called E untested. But UnlearnDiff is a discrete adversarial-prompt jailbreak, the kind of attack the catalog counts under E (compare Lucki et al.'s adapted GCG). Text-based E labels and a missing entry are added. SubAttack itself stays off E because it is an optimized continuous embedding; this is a judgement call.
(8) Missing: the Ring-A-Bell (Table 22) item is dropped because rows_left_out declares it. The STEREO item now names only F.
Judgement calls kept from the earlier verdict:
- The claim and its originals concern LLM knowledge unlearning; this is image-concept erasure in a diffusion model. It is linked as a T3 setting extension, though a reviewer may prefer fits_no_version.
- SubAttack is white-box and image-supervised, stronger than the 'simple attacks' in A, so it weighs less as a challenge to A.
- The F verdicts on SubDefense come from its own authors.
- ASR depends on imperfect classifiers (NudeNet, WikiArt top-3, ImageNet ResNet-50).
Inconsistencies in the paper:
- The Table 21 bases for FMN church (82.67%) and UCE Van Gogh (93.78%) differ from Table 8 (97.78% and 98.33%).
- ESD nudity NoAttack is 18.11% in Table 5 but 18.78% in Tables 3 and 8.
Section 4.1 says all victim models are fine-tuned from SD v1.4, though rows R25-R41 give their stage as not stated. The text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures image-generation ASR, not targeted-knowledge accuracy; it does not establish that each base unlearning method brings performance near chance while preserving general ability.
No test of fine-tuning the unlearned model on unrelated, loosely related, or subset-of-forgotten-facts examples.
The paper tests an interpretable residual in the token-embedding space and its projection, not ablation of an activation direction.
No recovery test using prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information alone.
SubDefense is tested against the paper's listed attacks, including SubAttack and UnlearnDiff; this is not an evaluation against every attack named in the claim.
